# configdirector_project (Resource)



## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    configdirector = {
      source  = "ConfigDirector/configdirector"
      version = "~> 0.2"
    }
  }
}

provider "configdirector" {}

resource "configdirector_project" "example" {
  name = "Project Example"
  slug = "project-example"
}

# Every project is created with "test" and "production" environments
# automatically - the API creates them, not Terraform, so they're surfaced
# here as read-only data rather than as separate resources. See the
# configdirector_environment example for adding more environments to a
# project.
output "environments" {
  value = configdirector_project.example.environments
}

output "organization_id" {
  value = configdirector_project.example.organization_id
}
```

## Deletion protection

While deletion protection is on for a project, or for any of its environments, destroying the project fails with an error that says where to turn it off. Deletion protection is turned on and off in the ConfigDirector dashboard, and Terraform reads it as `deletion_protection`. A project created in the dashboard, such as an organization's first project, starts with it on; one Terraform creates starts with it off.

Add `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` to a protected project to keep Terraform from planning its destroy:

```terraform
import {
  to = configdirector_project.storefront
  id = "storefront"
}

resource "configdirector_project" "storefront" {
  name = "Storefront"
  slug = "storefront"

  lifecycle {
    prevent_destroy = true
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String)
- `slug` (String)

### Read-Only

- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Whether deletion protection is on. It is set in the ConfigDirector dashboard; while on, destroying this resource fails. Pair it with `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }` to keep Terraform from planning the destroy.
- `environments` (Attributes Set) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--environments))
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `organization_id` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--environments"></a>
### Nested Schema for `environments`

Read-Only:

- `color` (String)
- `deletion_protection` (Boolean) Whether deletion protection is on for the environment. It is set in the ConfigDirector dashboard; while on, deleting the environment or its project fails.
- `id` (String)
- `live` (Boolean)
- `name` (String)
- `project_id` (String)
- `slug` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = configdirector_project.example
  id = "project-example"
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID can be either the project's UUID or its slug.
terraform import configdirector_project.example project-example
```
